findings.failure_path: Fan-out item 4 says to start with a few workers carrying several tasks each, while execution step 3 requires one bounded task per agent. A controller can follow the gate and produce multi-task workers whose ownership, deadline, and failed-return classification cannot be attributed to one bounded unit.
findings.smallest_fix: Replace "several tasks each" with wording consistent with one bounded slice per worker, optionally allowing several tightly related work items inside that single explicitly bounded slice.

findings.failure_path: The rule allows either running both pairwise orders or merely randomizing order, but then always requires an order-inconsistency rate and treatment of inconsistent pairs. A single randomized presentation per pair provides no counterfactual verdict, so that rate and denominator treatment cannot be computed and a release decision can rely on fabricated or undefined evidence.
findings.smallest_fix: Require both orders for every pair when reporting pair-level inconsistency; if only one randomized order is used, require an aggregate position-effect analysis and prohibit claiming an inconsistency rate.

findings.failure_path: Authorization 1 records a fresh wrapper plus at most one succession, but this file reinterprets the same human instruction as unbounded convergence rather than recording a new grant. That lets the controller authorize additional review/fix lanes beyond the documented scope.
findings.smallest_fix: Bind lane 2 to a separately recorded explicit human grant, or mark it unauthorized and rerun it only after such a grant; do not broaden the first grant by interpretation.

findings.failure_path: The added attestations bind only the base ref, while the supplied packet contains no final-candidate-bound command output. The profile reports make test on an earlier commit and treats size, zero-loss, and gate results as assertions, so later continuation edits could violate the 5000-word or repository gates while this release review remains falsely green.
findings.smallest_fix: Provide a controller-produced receipt bound to the exact candidate hash containing fresh outputs and exit statuses for check-size-budget.sh, check-ccl-skills.sh with the required base ref, and make test, plus enough candidate content to verify the zero-loss map.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: Not satisfied: the delegation rules contradict each other on tasks per worker, and the judge procedure permits a randomization design that cannot produce its required order-inconsistency metric.
The tool-revocation path is fail-closed, but the continuation record expands a previously bounded human authorization without a new explicit grant.

Revocation races and ambiguous batch submissions have explicit recovery paths; dispatch failure attribution remains ambiguous when the fan-out gate permits several tasks per worker despite the one-task rule.
Not satisfied: the bounded diff contains no final-candidate-bound outputs for the word budget, zero-loss mapping, skill checks, or make test; the profile claims make test only for an earlier commit.
The inference mutation boundary is consistent across its references, but the contradictory worker-granularity rules create an internal behavioral compatibility regression.
The documentation changes are mechanically revertible and describe version pinning, but the unsupported authorization expansion and missing candidate-bound gates block release readiness.
The diff adds concrete latency, goodput, cache, judge-agreement, and batch-reconciliation signals; no separate operational-visibility defect was found.
